record.field: Odoo holds a desired Stream Deck configuration for each workstation: the deck program, the plugins turned off and the settings of the deck service, its session refresh delay and the games; the key layout comes with lot 3b

streamdeck.config.line of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_config.py holds one setting per line, its key one of deck_program, plugins_off, session_refresh_sec and games (KEYS of streamdeck.config.schema), its value the canonical JSON that the schema validates.
The configuration comes from reusable profiles, from settings per deck model and from overrides per workstation

streamdeck.config.profile, streamdeck.config.model, one per USB product id, and the config_line_ids of streamdeck.workstation in ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_config.py; a workstation takes the profile of its config_profile_id and the model layers of its connected decks.
The priority goes from the profile to the deck model, then to the workstation; a setting the manager locks is not overridden by a lower layer
streamdeck.config.schema._effective folds the layers in that order and stops a key at the first layer that locks it; the reply lists the locked keys.
The employee sets the configuration within the manager's limits: the manager locks some settings, and the employee sets the others on their own workstations

The record rules of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/security/streamdeck_rules.xml give an employee the lines of their own workstations; streamdeck.config.line refuses an employee a key locked at any layer, and the fields locked and source.
A setting changed locally, through TODO › Stream Deck: Odoo offers a locked one again at the next report, and a free one goes up to Odoo as a new override of the workstation

_apply_config of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_service.py compares the local values with those last written to the file of the workstation (config_written): a locked key changed gives a new revision with the same values, a free key changed a workstation line of source local.
The employee confirms: the extension announces a new configuration and the employee clicks to apply it, which restarts the deck service

InventoryService.applyConfig of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory-service.js runs from a click only: the Apply action of the notification of extension.js, the entry of the deck menu of indicators/device.js, or the Apply button of the preferences through inventory-apply-request.

The extension receives the configuration with the report, applies it through the same paths as TODO › Stream Deck, the settings file and the restart of the deck service, and reports what is applied, or the refusal and its reason

rewriteConf of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/deck-config.js gives the bytes of settings_text of erplibre:script/todo/erplibre_home_service.py on the shared fixtures of test/fixtures/streamdeck_conf; the restart goes through the argv of lib/deck-service.js; the result rides the next report, and Odoo records it with a Configuration applied or Configuration refused event.
With several Odoo, the destination checked Pilot in the preferences pilots the workstation; no destination is the pilot by default

The GSettings key inventory-pilot of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:schemas holds the id of the pilot destination, empty by default; only that destination reads streamdeck.conf, sends a pilot body and has the configuration of its reply announced or applied.

At the first pilot, when free settings differ between the workstation and Odoo, the employee is asked whether to keep their local values, which become the overrides of the workstation, or to take Odoo's

Under the policy ask, the reply lists in ask the free managed keys whose local value is set and differs, until config_first_choice of the workstation is set; the extension asks in a notification, the deck menu and the preferences: Keep my settings writes nothing and sends the choice keep_local, Use Odoo's settings applies and sends take_odoo.

An organisation setting in Settings › Stream Deck lets the manager force the first-pilot choice: ask the employee, the default, keep the local values or take Odoo's; locked settings are offered for confirmation under every policy

streamdeck_first_pilot_policy of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/res_config_settings.py, stored as the ir.config_parameter erplibre_streamdeck.first_pilot_policy, ask by default and an unknown value read as ask; like every Stream Deck setting, only a Settings administrator writes it; under a forced policy a client choice counts for nothing, and a locked key is never in ask.

The decision gives the forcing to the Stream Deck manager, but only a Settings administrator writes the policy: res.config.settings is its only writer, and test_only_a_settings_administrator_sets_the_first_pilot_policy of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/tests/test_streamdeck_config_settings.py shows a Stream Deck manager without Settings rights refused. Left: a form under Stream Deck › Configuration with a write guard on the parameter, or a decision that names the Settings administrator.
Origin: violated; its unit test shows the violation.

The manager marks profiles selectable; the employee picks one of them for each of their workstations, the manager assigns any profile, and a profile that is not selectable is assigned by the manager alone

_check_profile_pick of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_workstation.py lets an employee set config_profile_id of their own workstation to an active selectable profile only, and only when the current one is empty or selectable; the form of the employee offers the selectable profiles and is read only on a profile the manager assigned.
A locked setting offered again follows the same path: a new revision that the employee confirms; nothing applies without a click
A local change of a locked key renews the revision with the same values in _apply_config; the extension announces it as any revision and writes nothing before applyConfig.

The settings Odoo sets are a closed list, the same on both sides of the wire, written in CONTRACT.md of the extension and held by tests in the three repositories: no path, no environment variable, no command, no plugin to turn on

CONFIG_KEYS of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/deck-config.js, KEYS and _validate of streamdeck.config.schema, and PROGRAMS, GAMES_VALUES, SESSION_REFRESH_RANGE and CONFIG_LINES of erplibre:script/todo/erplibre_home_service.py, each equal to the table of CONTRACT.md; plugins_off only turns plugins off.
The workstation checks every value against the schema before it writes; a value outside it refuses the whole revision with the reason invalid:<key>, and nothing is half written

validateConfig of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/deck-config.js refuses the whole configuration of a reply at its first key outside the schema, and rewriteConf throws before it builds anything; the inventory service reports the revision refused once and writes nothing.
Only the keys a layer sets are managed: a key no layer sets stays the employee's, locally, and Odoo never adopts it

The settings of the reply are those of _effective, the keys some layer sets; the adoption and the first-pilot question look at those keys only, and a workstation no layer configures gets no configuration.

The revision is computed at the report: Odoo takes a SHA-256 fingerprint of the canonical JSON of the effective configuration and moves the revision of the workstation when it changes, with no trigger on the layers
streamdeck.config.schema._hash; _apply_config compares it with config_hash of the workstation at each report and moves config_revision on a new fingerprint.
A revision already in place is not offered: when the file already holds Odoo's values, the extension reports it applied with no notification and no restart

_onConfig of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory-service.js reports applied a valid revision whose values the file holds and which carries no ask, unless a restart is still owed; an adopted override comes back that way and Odoo ends applied.
A workstation has one pilot destination; the other destinations receive its report and send no configuration back

A destination that is not the pilot sends config as pilot false; _parse_config of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_service.py answers it without configuration, and the extension applies the configuration of the pilot only.

The history gains four kinds that Odoo alone writes, a workstation that sends one getting 400: Configuration applied, Configuration refused, Local setting adopted and Setting changed locally; this lot opens no activity

SERVER_KINDS of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_event.py gains config_applied, config_refused, config_adopted and config_drift, with the revision, the keys and the reason; the history filters and shows them.

Profiles, deck models, one per USB product id and named from the known models, and lines carrying a key, a value, a lock, a source and exactly one parent among profile, deck model and workstation, one line per parent and key, each value checked by the schema of the workstation

streamdeck.config.profile, streamdeck.config.model and streamdeck.config.line of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_config.py: _check_one_parent, the SQL uniqueness per parent and key, and _check_value through streamdeck.config.schema._validate; the Configuration tab of the workstation shows its fields.

The effective configuration takes, for each key, the last layer that sets it, profile then deck model then workstation, stopping at the first layer that locks it; the deck models are those of the connected decks, by ascending USB product id, and the workstation warns when several apply

streamdeck.config.schema._layers and _effective of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_config.py; config_several_models of the workstation shows the warning on its Configuration tab.
Only the manager sets a lock, on a line of a profile, of a deck model or of a workstation
_check_employee_vals of streamdeck.config.line refuses locked and source to an employee, and a locked line keeps its key and value; the manager writes every layer.

The manager writes everything; an employee reads the profiles of their workstations, the selectable profiles and the deck model layers, writes the lines of their own workstations whose key no layer locks, never locked nor source, and never the state fields of the configuration, which the service alone writes

The access rights of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/security/ir.model.access.csv and the rules of security/streamdeck_rules.xml; the config_* state fields of the workstation are read only and written in sudo by streamdeck_service.py; the Configuration menus are the manager's.

A report in protocol 1.1 or later from a workstation with a managed key gets the configuration in its reply; a workstation in 1.0 stays unmanaged, and its form says the extension is too old to be piloted
_report of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_service.py reads config from protocol 1.1 on; config_too_old of the workstation reads its contract version below 1.3.

Odoo compares each managed key with the value it last wrote to the file: a locked key changed gives a Setting changed locally event and a new revision, a free key changed a workstation line of source local and a Local setting adopted event; before any application the first-pilot rule applies

_config_drift and _config_adopt of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/models/streamdeck_service.py measure against config_written, the values of the last revision written, and only when the report follows that revision; a free key cleared locally is offered again, never adopted.

Stream Deck › Configuration › Profiles and Deck models for the manager; a Configuration tab on the workstation with the profile, the effective table, the editable overrides, the state, the offered and applied revisions, the refusal reason and the pending date; the fleet filters the pending and refused configurations; in English and Canadian French

Anti-goal: an Odoo, or whoever controls it, that makes a workstation run code, write an arbitrary path or turn a plugin on

The closed list of CONTRACT.md: four keys, each a word of a list, ids turned off or a bounded number; the extension writes streamdeck.conf only, refuses a whole revision outside the schema and restarts the deck unit through a fixed argv.
Anti-goal: a configuration applied without the click of the employee
applyConfig and keepLocal of erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory-service.js are the only paths that write or answer, and each starts from a click; a reply only announces.
Anti-goal: a streamdeck.conf written halfway, or a line of the employee, a comment or an unmanaged key, lost at the write
rewriteConf keeps every byte outside the managed lines, and the write goes through a temporary file renamed over the target, removed on failure.
Anti-goal: two Odoo that fight over a workstation
One pilot destination at most, the inventory-pilot key; only its reply is announced or applied, and Odoo sends no configuration to a destination that is not the pilot.
Anti-goal: an employee who changes a locked setting in Odoo, or reads the configuration of another employee
The line guards of streamdeck.config.line, _check_profile_pick and the user rules of ERPLibre_erplibre_addons:erplibre_streamdeck/security/streamdeck_rules.xml.
Anti-goal: GNOME Shell blocked during the write or the restart
The application in erplibre-home-gnome-extension:lib/inventory-service.js is asynchronous from end to end, each step cut at TIMEOUT_S; GNOME Shell itself is checked on the manual checklist.
Anti-goal: identifying data in the code, the data, the comments or the commits

Examples are invented (host-a, SN-CFG, SN-PLUS); erplibre:script/analyse/check_comment_hygiene.py reports identifying data in comments, and the commit-msg hook of erplibre:script/git/hooks refuses an address, an email or an account path in a commit body.
No test sweeps the files of the control: check_comment_hygiene.py runs by hand and from the pre-commit hook, which lists its findings without blocking the commit.
